what-is-manual-testing.title: What is Manual Testing?
what-is-manual-testing.text1:
Manual Testing
The process of testing software applications by hand, without the use of automated tools. Testers manually execute test cases, simulating how an end-user would interact with the software, and verify the results against expected outcomes. This method is crucial for identifying defects and ensuring software quality before release.
Key Aspects:
  • No Automation
  • Exploratory Testing
  • Usability Testing
  • Regression Testing
  • Versatility
what-is-manual-testing.notes:
Manual Testing
  • Testing software witout automated tools
  • Simulate the end user
  • Verify results against an expected outcome
  • No code needs changed

what-is-automated-testing.title: What is Automated Testing?
what-is-automated-testing.text1:
Automated Testing
A software testing methodology that utilizes specialized tools and scripts to execute test cases and compare actual results against expected outcomes, with minimal or no human intervention during the execution phase. This contrasts with manual testing, where human testers manually interact with the software to identify defects.
Core Principles:
  • Test Script Creation
  • Automated Execution
  • Results Analysis
  • Unit Tests
  • Integration Tests
  • End-to-End Tests
what-is-automated-testing.notes:
Automated Testing
  • Specialized software and scripts
  • Executes specific test cases
  • Results analysis by a person
  • Levels: Unit Tests, Integration Tests, End-to-End Tests, ...

what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.title: What is Non-Automated Automated Testing?
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.text1:
Non-Automated Automated Testing
This is a term that I started using when a production deployment went sideways for an "odd reason."
Production deployments often use hybrid approaches:
  • Automated tests run to verify key functionality.
  • Humans perform contextual verification/checks that automation cannot fully capture.
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.text2:
Definition:
Automated test tools (or scripts) are used to initiate and carry out predefined checks in the live production environment.
The execution is complemented by manual steps that cannot be fully automated:
  • Triggering jobs.
  • Validating test data
  • Interpreting results.
  • Performing exploratory checks.
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.notes:
Non-Automated Automated Testing
  • Prod deployment went sideways
  • Pre and Post Automation with a heavy amount of "human contextual verification that automation" cannot fully capture
  • "Automated test tools (or scripts) are used to initiate and carry out predefined checks in the live production environment."

what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.title: What is Non-Automated Automated Testing?
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.text1:
Non-Automated Automated Testing
This is a term that I started using when a production deployment went sideways for an "odd reason."
Production deployments often use hybrid approaches:
  • Automated tests run to verify key functionality.
  • Humans perform contextual verification/checks that automation cannot fully capture.
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.text2:
Automation Ensures:
Consistent, repeatable coverage of known requirements, while human testers provide contextual judgment, visual validation, and decision-making before, during, or after the automated tests are run.
The combined approach aims to quickly detect production issues and confirm deployment success while accounting for real-world conditions automation alone may miss.

workflow-automation-original.title: Functional VRT
workflow-automation-original.notes:
As I originally implemented the non-automated automted tests ...
  1. Run the scan with no images stored. It stored the images for later use.
  2. DEPLOY: Run the scan with images in place. Images that are over the threshold are marked and can be reviewed.
      3. This all runs on a single machine (one user).

workflow-automation-pipelines.title: Functional Pipeline & VRT
workflow-automation-pipelines.notes:
More automation for the non-automated automted tests ...
  1. Run the scan with no images stored (on ADO; cron - 8 pm daily). It stored the images for later use (by Zipping them up and storing them in a bucket).
  2. DEPLOY: Run the scan (manual trigger in ADO) with images in place (pull images from the bucket). Images that are over the threshold are marked and can be reviewed.
      3. This all runs through a pipeline and has a link and page at the end of the cycle for "team-level review".

what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.title: Why use Non-Automated Automated Testing?
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.text1:
Concise Definition
Non-automated automated testing (in production) is a hybrid testing approach where automated tools execute predefined test actions against a live deployment, but human testers manually initiate, observe, interpret, and supplement these actions with additional checks to validate real-world behavior before finalizing the release as successful.
what-is-non-automated-automated-testing-.text2:
Why use it?
  • Automation is fast and repeatable, but blind to qualitative, visual, and contextual nuances.
  • Manual testing is adaptable and insightful, especially when production data or environments behave differently than staging.
  • In production deployments, risk tolerance is low, so blending automation with human oversight reduces false negatives and false positives.

points-of-failure.title: Common Risks & Failure
points-of-failure.text1:
1. Human dependency & Variability: Missed defects, slower execution, unpredictable quality sign-offs.
  2. Misinterpretation of automated results: false positives or negatives.
  3. Automation drift: false sense of coverage; critical paths go untested.
  4. Critical-path blind spots: Undetected defects in the most important user flows.
